iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max are arriving tomorrow (here's our review), and Apple also plans to put the new devices to use this Friday during its 'Friday Night Baseball' broadcast, featuring a matchup between the Giants and the Dodgers. Here are the details.

How Apple will use the iPhone 18 Pro during this Friday's 'Friday Night Baseball' broadcast

Last fall, the iPhone 17 Pro made history as the first smartphone used to produce a live broadcast of a professional sports event. Four iPhone 17 Pro units were used to capture unique angles, and the National Baseball Hall of Fame has since added one of them to its collection in New York.

Now, riding the momentum of the iPhone 18 Pro launch, Apple plans to take things a step further during this Friday's 'Friday Night Baseball' broadcast.

Tomorrow evening, September 18 at 7:15 p.m. Pacific Time, the final 'Friday Night Baseball' broadcast of the season will deploy 14 iPhone 18 Pro units to deliver live coverage of the San Francisco Giants hosting the Los Angeles Dodgers.

The iPhone 18 Pro units will be positioned throughout Dodger Stadium, including the pitch timer, the netting behind home plate, the foul poles, and both teams' bullpens, giving viewers unique angles that conventional broadcast cameras can't capture.

Of the 14 iPhone 18 Pro units, 8 will transmit live footage directly to the broadcast using T-Mobile's dedicated 5G private network. Beyond the game itself, the iPhone 18 Pro will also capture batting practice, player introductions, dugout perspectives, and other standout moments.

All Apple TV subscribers can watch 'Friday Night Baseball' for free.

Apple TV costs $14.99 per month, with additional savings available through Apple One bundles.
